title: Query Node Health Events
description: Query `k8s_node`-level logs (kubelet, node-problem-detector, TPU device plugin) for the nodes of a workload. Complements [[query-vm-termination-events]], which reads GCE audit logs and therefore sees only interventions made at the GCE layer: a worker killed inside the node -- for example a SIGILL with `si_code=0`, meaning SI_USER, delivered via kill() by another process -- leaves the audit log completely clean. When [[ai-hw-analyzer]] is asked to weigh in-node evidence against a clean audit result, this is the action that produces it. Scoping is mandatory and is done with the `node_name_filter_clause` from [[resolve-workload-nodes]], NOT the `node_filter_clause`: the latter matches `protoPayload.resourceName`, a field that exists only on audit entries. A k8s_node query has neither that field nor a pod_name, so an unscoped run silently returns other workloads' container kills on other clusters and invites a false in-node verdict. For 1,000+ node workloads where `node_name_filter_clause` would exceed Cloud Logging's 20,000-character limit, `pull_and_format_logs.py` automatically compacts >400-node / >18,000-character `resource.labels.node_name` lists into node-pool prefix filters (`resource.labels.node_name:"<pool>-"`); you may also scope `node_filter` specifically to candidate culprit nodes from [[extract-culprit-hosts]]. If `original_count` equals `limit` the query saturated and the result is truncated: narrow `filter_extra` and re-run before drawing any negative conclusion from it.

node_filter.description: The `node_name_filter_clause` emitted by [[resolve-workload-nodes]] (or a scoped `(resource.labels.node_name="<node>" OR ...)` clause for candidate culprit nodes on 1,000+ node runs; `pull_and_format_logs.py` also auto-compacts >400-node / >18,000-char clauses into node-pool prefixes). REQUIRED. A k8s_node query carries no pod_name label, so without this clause the query is not scoped to the workload at all and returns the whole project's node logs -- other workloads on other clusters.

start.description: Window start (RFC3339). Required to reach a historical incident: without it gcloud applies its default 1-day freshness and returns nothing.

filter_extra.default: \"node-problem-detector\" OR \"NodeNotReady\" OR \"KernelDeadlock\" OR \"OOMKilling\" OR \"Killing container\" OR \"Unhealthy\" OR \"FailedKillPod\" OR \"SystemOOM\" OR \"TaskHung\" OR \"tpu-device-plugin\"
filter_extra.description: Log filter expression. The default is restricted to problem indicators; broad terms such as "kubelet" or "TPU" match routine node chatter, saturate the entry cap, and hide the events worth seeing.

output_file.description: Output path for the queried logs.

limit.description: Log read limit. The script defaults to 100, which silently truncates a whole-window sweep.
